data.productDescription: Dry weight of herbaceous vegetation harvested from individual clip strips, by functional type
data.productAbstract:
This data product contains the quality-controlled, native sampling resolution data from NEON's Herbaceous biomass clip harvest sampling. Herbaceous vegetation is operationally defined in this protocol as non-woody plants (i.e. grasses, sedges, forbs, some bryophytes, and non-woody vines such as Convolvulus spp. and certain Rubus spp.), as well as woody-stemmed plants with diameter at decimeter height (ddh) < 1 cm at the time of sampling. For additional details, see the user guide, protocols, and science design listed in the Documentation section in this data product's details webpage.

Latency:
The expected time from data and/or sample collection in the field to data publication is as follows, for each of the data tables (in days) in the downloaded data package. See the Data Product User Guide for more information.

hbp_massdata:  60

hbp_perbout:  60
data.productDesignDescription: Clip-harvest of herbaceous biomass occurs within randomly located clip-harvest strips in 20m x 20m plots or subplots. Up to 20 non-forested Distributed plots (containing 1 clip strip per plot) and up to 30 Tower plots (containing 1-4 clip strips per plot) are sampled at each site. Tower plots are sampled every year at sites where herbaceous productivity > 10% of the sum of herbaceous and woody productivity. Tower plots at ungrazed sites are sampled once per year if there is a single annual biomass peak, and twice at sites with two biomass peaks per year in order to capture both warm season and cool season production. At grazed sites, sampling in Tower plots occurs once every 4 or 8 weeks while livestock are present. Distributed plots are sampled once every 5 years at plots where herbaceous aerial cover ≥ 50% at the plot scale.
data.productStudyDescription:
These data are collected at NEON terrestrial sites.

Data collection for the Herbaceous clip harvest at Distributed plots was suspended in 2026, leading to a 6-year interval between sampling events rather than the expected 5-year interval. The annual sampling at Tower plots is unaffected by this change and will be carried out in 2026 as usual. Distributed plot sampling originally scheduled for 2026 will be implemented in 2027, and the schedule originally intended for 2027 will be implemented in 2028 and so forth, leading to a consistent 6-year interval between sampling events across all sites in the schedule until 2032.
data.productBasicDescription: The basic download package includes all measurements. An expanded download package is not available for this product.
data.productRemarks: Queries for this data product for `hbp_perbout` and `hbp_massdata` files will be subset to data collected during the date range specified. A given `hbp_perbout.clipID` is expected to be sampled zero or one times per collectDate (local time). A record from `hbp_perbout` may have zero or more child records in `hbp_massdata`, depending on whether or not herbaceous material is present in the selected clip cell (indicated by the `hbp_perbout.targetTaxaPresent` field), whether clipped material was sorted to functional group (`hbp_massdata.herbGroup`), and whether reweighing occurred for QA purposes (`hbp_massdata.qaDryMass`). Duplicates may exist where protocol and/or data entry aberrations have occurred; users should check data carefully for anomalies before joining tables.

changeLogs.issue: Sampling timing updated: Distributed plot sampling on three-year intervals was not aligned with sampling and data collection for other plant biomass and productivity data products.
changeLogs.resolution: Interannual sampling schedule changed to five-year intervals to coincide with other plant biomass and productivity data products.

changeLogs.locationAffected: All terrestrial sites managed for grazing
changeLogs.issue: Grazing sampling reduced: Consultation with the external Technical Working Group guided statistical analyses that resulted in data-driven sampling reductions at sites managed for grazing.
changeLogs.resolution: Prior to the 2018 sampling season, all sites managed for grazing were sampled for herbaceous biomass on a 4-week interval. The design modification increased the sampling interval from 4-weeks to 8-weeks at moderately productive sites where consumption could not be detected with a 4-week interval. At grazed sites with minimal productivity, sampling was reduced to 1 or 2 bouts per year; exclosures at these sites allow an assessment of relative grazing intensity but possibly not consumption.

changeLogs.issue: Sampling number reduced: Consultation with the external Technical Working Group guided statistical analyses that resulted in data-driven sampling reductions at Tower plots.
changeLogs.resolution: Prior to the 2018 sampling season, all Tower plots were sampled during each bout at each site. The design modification reduced the number of Tower plots at specific sites to a sample size that maintains the capacity to detect a 20% change in interannual herbaceous biomass productivity based on three or more years of data.

changeLogs.issue: New sampling method: At select grazed sites, the bouts not associated with peak biomass during which harvested samples are not sorted by functional group, all biomass clipped was collected and weighed. In specific systems the process was time consuming and difficult.
changeLogs.resolution: Experimental investigation, statistical analysis and consultation with the external Technical Working Group resulted in a subsampling approach: part of the plot-specific clip harvest is dried and weighed but data-driven estimates of the entire sample mass are reported.

changeLogs.issue: Functional group change: Samples were sorted to functional groups that included the category 'Leguminous Forbs (LFB)' but qualifying individuals were not limited to forbs.
changeLogs.resolution: Leguminous forbs and nitrogen fixers < 1 cm decimeter height are sorted to the 'N-fixer (NFX)' functional group category.

changeLogs.issue: No sampling impractical: Prior to 2020, there was no mechanism to communicate that fewer than the targeted number plots were sampled.
changeLogs.resolution: In 2020, NEON added the quality flag **samplingImpractical** to the `hbp_perbout` table – to indicated when field sampling did not occur – and `hbp_massdata` table – to indicate when collected samples could not be processed - to assist users in understanding when data for this product are temporarily missing versus permanently unavailable. Beginning in 2020, there will always be one record generated for each plot scheduled for sampling in the `hbp_perbout` table. If **samplingImpractical** is set to 'OK' in the `hbp_perbout` table, there will always be a corresponding record generated in the `hbp_massdata` table. For example, if field sampling was not possible **samplingImpractical** is populated with a value other than 'OK' (e.g., 'location flooded') in the `hbp_perbout` table, no sample is generated, and no record is generated in the `hbp_massdata` table. If **samplingImpractical** is set to 'OK' in the `hbp_perbout` table there will be a corresponding record in the `hbp_massdata` table, but **samplingImpractical** in the `hbp_massdata` table is populated with a value other than 'OK' if that sample could not be processed.

changeLogs.issue: Determine sampling timing: Prior to 2020, there was no mechanism to communicate when sampling did not occur at peak biomass.
changeLogs.resolution: In 2020, NEON added the quality flag **biophysicalCriteria** to the `hbp_perbout` table to assist users in understanding that data for this product was collected when conditions were not optimal. If conditions were suboptimal – biomass was not at peak - the field **biophysicalCriteria** is populated with a value other than 'OK - no known exceptions' but the sample is generated.

changeLogs.issue: Safety measures to protect personnel during the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in reduced or canceled sampling activities for extended periods at NEON sites. Data availability may be reduced during this time.
changeLogs.resolution: The primary impact of the pandemic on observational data was reduced data collection. Training procedures and data quality reviews were maintained throughout the pandemic, although some previously in-person training was conducted virtually.  Scheduled measurements and sampling that were not carried out due to COVID-19 or any other causes are indicated in data records via the samplingImpractical data field.

changeLogs.issue: Toolik Field Station required a quarantine period prior to starting work in the 2020, 2021, and 2022 field seasons to protect all personnel during the COVID-19 pandemic. This complicated NEON field scheduling logistics, which typically involves repeated travel across the state on short time frames. Consequently, NEON reduced staffing traveling to Toolik and was thus unable to complete all planned sampling efforts. Missed data collection events are indicated in data records via the samplingImpractical field.
changeLogs.resolution: The quarantine policy at Toolik Field Station ended after the 2022 field season.

changeLogs.issue: Severe flooding destroyed several roads into Yellowstone National Park in June 2022, making the YELL and BLDE sites inaccessible to NEON staff. Observational data collection was halted during this time. Canceled data collection events are indicated in data records via the samplingImpractical field.
changeLogs.resolution: Normal operations resumed on October 31, 2022, when the National Park Service opened a newly constructed road from Gardiner, MT to Mammoth, WY with minimal restrictions. For more details about data impacts, see Data Notification https://www.neonscience.org/impact/observatory-blog/data-impacts-neons-yellowstone-sites-yell-blde-due-catastrophic-flooding-0

changeLogs.issue: Misreported bryophyte masses: Sampling years prior to 2022, clip harvests of bryophytes at the affected site included small and epiphytic material not intended for collection per the protocol (NEON.DOC.014037) due to the modest contribution to biomass stocks and the amount of effort to complete these collections. Reported bryophyte masses are likely slightly inflated for this site prior to 2022.
changeLogs.resolution: Clarified that bryophytes included in clip harvest should focus on mat-forming morphologies and those that substantially contribute to biomass stocks e.g., sphagnum, boreal feather, and cushion mosses.

changeLogs.issue: New bryophyte method: Prior to the 2022 sampling season, harvesting and sorting all bryophyte material from the current-year clipped biomass at a subset of sites resulted in prolonged sampling collection events due to high density of herbaceous material.
changeLogs.resolution: To reduce the time associated with sorting bryophytes from the current-year herbaceous material, a 25% subsample is sorted at HEAL, BONA, DEJU, and a 50% subsample is sorted at BARR and TOOL. Mass ratios are then calculated to deliver end users calculated estimates of dried, current-year mass.

changeLogs.issue: Ended grazing SOP, TEAK: The grazing SOP (SOP C) was relevant to only plot - TEAK_051 – at TEAK in Domain 17. During the 2021 sampling season it was determined that the density of downed logs limited the number of locations exclosure sampling could take place and also reduced and likely eliminated the capacity of cattle to access herbaceous material in the plot.
changeLogs.resolution: Given the difficulty of sampling, the limited impact of grazing, and that the grazing SOP was implemented at only one plot, the grazing SOP has been eliminated from TEAK_051.

changeLogs.issue: Publishing oven dates: drying oven in and out dates will now be published in the hbp_massdata table. These fields provide time stamps for when drying occurred relative to sample collection and can provide useful insight into total lab processing times. Publishing these data aligns with other NEON data products where samples are processed in NEON laboratories.
changeLogs.resolution: The ovenStartDate and ovenEndDate is published in all provisional data and will be published in RELEASE-2024 and onwards.  These fields are not present in earlier releases up to and including RELEASE-2023.

changeLogs.issue: SubplotId change: The Base plot subplot naming convention was ambiguous with respect to location and scale, and not well differentiated from the identifiers of the points that spatially define Base plots.
changeLogs.resolution: The subplot naming convention is updated across all data products with observations and samples that originate from Base plots. The format consists of the identity of the plot point in the southwest corner of the subplot, the scale or size of the subplot, and, for those subplots smaller than 100 m2, the corner of the 100 m2 subplot in which the smaller subplot is located. For example, ‘21_400’ refers to point 21 in the southwest corner and is 400 m2 (20 m x 20 m), and ‘31_1_1’ is a subplot with point 31 in the southwest corner, is 1 m2, and is in corner 1 of the 100 m2 subplot with point 31 in the southwest corner. See the associated Data Notification for further detail: https://www.neonscience.org/impact/observatory-blog/neon-terrestrial-observation-system-tos-base-plot-subplot-renaming.

changeLogs.locationAffected: BART, LENO, SERC, HARV, ORNL, PUUM, UNDE, DELA, GUAN, SCBI, WREF
changeLogs.issue: Sampling threshold not met: Herbaceous vegetation is < 10% of productivity at the tower plots of 11 sites, based on an analysis of data collected through 2021. The NEON Science Design indicates that vegetation components that are > 10% cover (or in this case productivity) should be sampled. In the interest of reducing labor costs spent on sampling not required by the Science Design, the Productivity Technical Working Group agreed that it would be acceptable to suspend sampling at the tower plots of 11 sites where herbaceous aboveground productivity is < 10% of the sum of aboveground herbaceous and woody productivity.
changeLogs.resolution: Starting in 2023, herbaceous clip harvest sampling has been suspended at the tower plots of 11 sites (BART, LENO, SERC, HARV, ORNL, PUUM, UNDE, DELA, GUAN, SCBI, and WREF) where herbaceous aboveground productivity is < 10% of the sum of aboveground herbaceous and woody productivity.

changeLogs.issue: Publishing oven dates: drying oven in and out dates will now be published in the hbp_massdata table. These fields provide time stamps for when drying occurred relative to sample collection and can provide useful insight into total lab processing times. Publishing these data aligns with other NEON data products where samples are processed in NEON laboratories.
changeLogs.resolution: The ovenStartDate and ovenEndDate is published in all provisional data and will be published in RELEASE-2024 and onwards.  These fields are not present in earlier releases up to and including RELEASE-2023.

changeLogs.issue: Add new ‘sampleCondition’ field to hbp_massdata table. SampleCondition is a new field that will be published in the hbp_massdata table. This field provides insight into the integrity of each subsample created and subsequently processed in the laboratory. Publishing these data aligns with other NEON data products where samples are processed in NEON laboratories.
changeLogs.resolution: The 'sampleCondition' field will be published in all data starting from 02/01/2024 onwards.

changeLogs.locationAffected: DCFS, NOGP, WOOD, CLBJ, ONAQ, SJER
changeLogs.issue: New old standing dead method: Prior to the 2023 sampling season, harvesting and sorting all old standing dead (OSD) material from the current-year herbaceous masses at a subset of sites resulted in prolonged sample collection and processing events due to the high density of herbaceous material.
changeLogs.resolution: To reduce the time associated with sorting OSD from target material, a 25% subsample is sorted at the locations affected.  Mass ratios are then calculated to deliver data that reflect estimates of dried, current-year masses as if the entire clip strip was processed and weighed.

changeLogs.issue: Delayed sampling: Data collection for the distributed plot component of Herbaceous clip harvest was suspended in 2026, leading to a 6-year interval between sampling events, rather than the usual 5-year interval. The annual sampling of tower plots is unaffected by this change and will be carried out in 2026 as usual. This suspension was implemented due to unusual budget demands in 2026. For more details, see https://www.neonscience.org/impact/observatory-blog/2026-product-modifications.
changeLogs.resolution: Distributed plot sampling will resume in 2027, using the schedule originally intended for 2026. The schedule originally intended for 2027 will be carried out in 2028, and so forth, leading to a consistent 6-year interval between sampling events across all sites, until 2032.

changeLogs.issue: NEON Operations ended at the Dead Lake (DELA) terrestrial site in the fall of 2025, at the request of the site host. Instrument Systems (IS) data collection discontinued as of Oct. 6, 2025, and Observation Systems (OS) data collection discontinued as of Dec 31, 2025. Airborne Observation Platform (AOP) data will continue to be collected. For more details, see  https://www.neonscience.org/impact/observatory-blog/neon-operations-coming-close-dead-lake-alabama-field-site.
changeLogs.resolution: All data and samples collected at DELA up until the site decommissioning will remain available on the NEON Data Portal and Biorepository Data Portal for the lifetime of NEON.
